decisions.decision: Clean project. M2 targets exactly one pre-existing, empty Google Cloud project per installation, named al-<installation_id>-live, where the project id satisfies ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{5,29}$ and installation_id appears as a hyphen-delimited segment of it (so installation_id is at most 21 characters). Region defaults to us-central1. Enabled services are exactly the six unconditional APIs already declared in infra/main.tf locals.apis (artifactregistry, firestore, iap, run, serviceusage, iamcredentials), plus cloudscheduler only when the cost-gated scheduler is enabled, plus cloudresourcemanager which the data google_project number lookup requires. Four things infra/ deliberately does not create are human preconditions and must exist before the first plan: the Artifact Registry repository together with the digest-pinned image, the IAP brand/OAuth consent screen, the Cloud Storage bucket that holds OpenTofu state, and the billing link with an approved budget. 'Empty' is defined as all of the following, each observed read-only and recorded in the preflight record before apply: project lifecycleState is ACTIVE; zero Cloud Run services in the region; no Firestore database at all, in particular no (default); zero composite Firestore indexes; zero Cloud Scheduler jobs; no service account besides the Google-managed defaults; no IAM binding whose member matches agentic-loop-*; and an OpenTofu state that lists no resources. Separation of production from test resources is by project, not by name prefix: this project holds only the control plane, and any destructive or sandbox exercise belongs to a separate al-<installation_id>-lab project which is explicitly out of M2 scope.
decisions.rationale: infra/variables.tf states the module never creates a project and never creates the Artifact Registry repository, and google_firestore_database carries deletion_policy = ABANDON together with prevent_destroy, so the first apply permanently ends the project's emptiness; a second clean-project exercise therefore requires a brand-new project rather than a destroy. Naming the project after installation_id keeps the canonical record namespace, the IAP owner boundary and the billing boundary from drifting apart, and a hyphen-delimited segment rule can be machine-checked without forbidding an already-provisioned project whose name differs in suffix. Every emptiness observation is read-only so that the check that guards the side effect cannot itself cost money or mutate the target.

decisions.decision: Budget. The hard budget is 50 percent of the Firestore always-free daily allowance recorded in docs/operations/gcp-runbook.md on 2026-08-22 (50,000 reads, 20,000 writes, 20,000 deletes per day, 1 GiB stored): 25,000 reads/day, 10,000 writes/day, 10,000 deletes/day, and 536,870,912 stored bytes, of which the enforced document-payload ceiling is 268,435,456 bytes because Firestore also bills index storage and this design assumes at most a 2x index overhead. Cloud Run is capped at 50 percent of the monthly free tier (90,000 vCPU-seconds, 180,000 GiB-seconds, 1,000,000 requests); at the pinned cpu = 0.08 and memory = 512Mi the binding ceiling is 360,000 billable instance-seconds per month (the CPU bound would be 1,125,000), and requests are capped at 1,000,000 per month. Cloud Scheduler is capped at zero jobs: enable_reconcile_scheduler stays false for M2. Measured gap that V2-013 must close: internal/quota.DefaultBudget is 40,000/16,000/16,000, which is 80 percent, not 50 percent, so the current code cannot satisfy the M2 completion condition; and the flat worst-case reservation makes the plane unusable at any percentage, because ReadTransactionUsage reserves 6,001 reads per read transaction, which measured out at 6 read transactions per day at 80 percent and 4 per day at 50 percent (1,000 and 625 mutations per day respectively). The fix is not to raise the ceiling but to keep the fail-closed pre-check on the conservative worst case and then true up the staged quota delta to the actual operation count before the transaction flushes, using the reads already recorded in the unit-of-work cache and the staged writes and deletes. There is no storage accounting at all today (measured: internal/quota has no bytes or storage symbol), so a stored-bytes accumulator that is a level rather than a daily flow must be added, incremented by the serialized payload delta of staged documents, decremented on delete, and enforced before staging. Over-budget behaviour: quota.ErrOverBudget must surface as HTTP 429 with error code quota_exhausted and a Retry-After pointing at the next UTC midnight, and the affected work must become an explicit waiting or needs-input state; today it is unmapped and falls through internal/api.domainError to 400 invalid_request (measured), which reports a capacity exhaustion as a caller mistake.
decisions.rationale: docs/architecture/roadmap.md M2 requires not exceeding 50 percent of the Firestore free quota, and docs/policies/README.md requires budgets to be enforced before the side effect and requires exhaustion to become explicit waiting or needs-input rather than success. A reservation made inside the same transaction before any mutation is staged satisfies 'before the side effect'; truing up to the actual count in the same transaction does not weaken that guarantee, because the pre-check still refuses the worst case, and it is what makes a 50 percent ceiling survivable. Storage is a level, not a flow, so it cannot share the daily counter that resets at UTC midnight. Mapping exhaustion to 400 would make a budget stop indistinguishable from a malformed request, which is exactly the 'never reported as success, always explicit' rule inverted into an unactionable signal.

decisions.decision: Apply, verify, rollback. Apply is five ordered steps, each with fixed argv: (1) devbox run --pure -- scripts/infra-policy.sh; (2) TFVARS_FILE=<absolute path outside the repository> devbox run --pure -- scripts/infra-plan.sh, which writes infra/build/infra.tfplan; (3) devbox run --pure -- tofu -chdir=infra show -json build/infra.tfplan redirected to infra/build/infra.plan.json, then sha256sum of that file, which becomes target.plan_digest in the preflight record; (4) a human approves that exact digest and the approval is committed as the preflight record; (5) cd infra && tofu apply -input=false build/infra.tfplan, applying the saved plan artifact and nothing else. Verify is read-only and all of: tofu plan -refresh-only -detailed-exitcode exits 0, meaning no drift (exit 2 means drift and fails the step); the Cloud Run service reports min_instance_count 0, max_instance_count 1, concurrency 1, cpu 0.08, memory 512Mi, cpu_idle true, iap_enabled true and the digest-pinned image; an unauthenticated HTTPS request to the service URI returns 302 or 403 and never 200; an authenticated owner request through IAP returns 200 from /healthz; the Firestore (default) database is FIRESTORE_NATIVE in the configured location and exactly the two composite indexes of infra/indexes.tf exist; no Cloud Scheduler job exists; and the daily quota document totals are at or below the d2 ceilings and are greater than or equal to the read/write/delete counts observed in Cloud Monitoring for the same UTC day, which is what proves the guard is binding rather than decorative. Rollback is revision rollback, not resource deletion: set image_digest back to the last known-good 64-hex digest, re-plan, obtain a new approval for the new plan digest, and apply the new saved plan. Rollback is complete only when all of these hold: 100 percent of traffic is served by the revision built from the previous digest; tofu plan -refresh-only -detailed-exitcode exits 0; /healthz returns 200 through IAP; and a sampled read of canonical Firestore documents has the same content digest as before the rollback. Resource-level rollback does not exist by design and must not be attempted: google_firestore_database and google_cloud_run_v2_service both carry prevent_destroy, the Cloud Run service also carries deletion_protection = true, and the database carries deletion_policy = ABANDON, which together mean tofu destroy fails, and that if the database resource were ever removed from configuration or state the real database would be left running in the project rather than deleted. Consequences to state in the runbook: no data is lost by a rollback, the project can never be returned to the empty state by OpenTofu, a re-apply after a state loss requires tofu import rather than create, tofu state rm must never be used to bypass the protection, and emergency deletion needs its own approval, state backup and impact record.
decisions.rationale: docs/policies/README.md requires an idempotent apply path, read-only drift detection, verification and rollback for every external dependency, and forbids console-only truth. Applying a saved plan artifact is the only way the thing a human approved and the thing that executed are provably the same object; the existing .github/workflows/deploy.yml instead runs tofu apply -auto-approve -var-file=..., which re-plans at apply time and can therefore apply something nobody approved. -detailed-exitcode is required because scripts/infra-drift.sh currently exits 0 whether or not drift exists, so drift is reported to a human but never fails a gate. The negative IAP probe is included because docs/operations/control-plane-production.md makes non-public exposure a deployment invariant, and an invariant with no negative test is an assumption. Comparing the app's own quota totals against Cloud Monitoring counters is the only way to show that the reservation is conservative in the correct direction.

decisions.decision: Scale-to-zero. Idle is defined as a continuous 20-minute window in which zero requests reach the service and no reconcile trigger fires; 20 minutes is chosen because Cloud Run may keep an instance for roughly 15 minutes after the last request. Scale-to-zero is proven read-only from Cloud Monitoring over that window, not from the Cloud Run description: the metric run.googleapis.com/container/instance_count filtered to the service, aligned at 60 seconds and aggregated with MAX, must be 0 for both state=active and state=idle, and the metric run.googleapis.com/container/billable_instance_time summed over the same window must be 0. Both are read through the Cloud Monitoring v3 timeSeries.list endpoint with curl and a short-lived workload-identity access token, because gcloud is absent from the pinned environment; if the executor substitutes an equivalent gcloud or API surface, the evidence must record the argv actually executed and the metric names actually used, never the assumed ones. That the optional Cloud Scheduler does not force an always-on instance is verified in two layers: for M2, enable_reconcile_scheduler is false, the applied plan JSON contains no google_cloud_scheduler_job resource, and the project lists zero scheduler jobs; and for any future enablement, the arithmetic is recorded in the runbook: a bounded tick is at most 30 seconds of active time (docs/architecture/validation.md section 5), so */5 costs 8,928 ticks times 30 seconds equals 267,840 instance-seconds per month, which is 74 percent of the 360,000-second ceiling in d2 and leaves too little for owner traffic, whereas */15 costs 2,976 ticks equals 89,280 seconds, which is 25 percent. The default of var.reconcile_schedule therefore becomes */15, and enabling the job still additionally requires reconcile_cost_preflight_approved and a custom IAP audience, both already enforced as lifecycle preconditions.
decisions.rationale: Instance count is not a field of the Cloud Run service resource, so a describe call can only show the configured min and max, never the observed zero; only the time series can show that no instance was running while nothing was being served, and billable_instance_time is the metric that ties the observation directly to cost. Cloud Scheduler at a 5-minute cadence would not literally pin an instance, but it would consume three quarters of the approved compute ceiling with no user-visible work, which is the same failure the ceiling exists to prevent, so the honest fix is the cadence default rather than a claim that the cost is negligible. Requiring the executor to record the argv it really ran keeps an unavailable CLI from silently becoming an unverified assertion.

decisions.decision: Preflight record form. Add one new contract, contracts/schemas/deployment-preflight.json ($id deployment-preflight-v1), rather than overloading evidence.json or work-order.json, and store instances at .agents/v2/preflight/<task_id>-<purpose>.json. Required fields: schema_version const v1; id; kind const deployment-preflight; created_at; correlation_id; task_id matching ^V2-[0-9]{3}$; target with environment (enum live, lab), project_ref, installation_id, region, service_name, image_digest and plan_digest, the last two matching ^[a-f0-9]{64}$; limits, a non-empty array of objects with resource, ceiling, unit, window (enum day, month, total), enforced_by and fail_closed const true; rollback with trigger, argv and a non-empty completion_conditions array; verification, a non-empty array of objects with name, argv, expected and read_only; and approval with approver (email form), approved_at, approval_reference and scope. Optional: expires_at and notes. additionalProperties is false everywhere, and the schema text must not contain the substrings password, credential, raw_prompt or raw_provider_output, which TestSchemasRejectSensitiveFieldNames enforces across contracts/schemas. A new test in internal/contracts enforces the invariant that human approval precedes the side effect, and it must pass in the V2-013 state where no preflight record and no live evidence exist yet: every file under .agents/v2/preflight/ validates against the schema and its filename begins with its task_id; project_ref starts with al- and contains installation_id as a hyphen-delimited segment when environment is live; every limits entry has fail_closed true and the resource set covers at least firestore-reads-per-day, firestore-writes-per-day, firestore-deletes-per-day, firestore-stored-bytes, cloud-run-instance-seconds-per-month, cloud-run-requests-per-month and cloud-scheduler-jobs; and for every entry of .agents/v2/evidence/index.json whose component begins with gcp-live- there is exactly one preflight record with the same task_id, the evidence carries an artifact_refs entry whose artifact_id is deployment-preflight and whose sha256 equals the sha256 of that record file, and approval.approved_at is strictly earlier than the evidence observed_at. Consequently a live evidence record with no matching approved preflight record fails the ledger test, which is the mechanical form of the invariant.
decisions.rationale: Neither existing schema can carry a checkable approval: evidence.json has additionalProperties false with no approver, approval time or ceiling field, and its checks[].summary is free text; work-order.json constraints are free strings. A free-text claim of approval is not an invariant. Binding the approval to plan_digest, and the live evidence to the record's file digest, makes the approved object and the executed object the same artifact rather than two descriptions of one intention. Fixtures and the new test are the whole test cost, and no change to ci/components.json is needed because contracts/**, internal/contracts/** and .agents/** already have owning components, which matters because touching ci/components.json would invalidate every component evidence key.

decisions.decision: Local and live boundary. V2-013 is local-closed and may claim only: make check green including the Firestore emulator integration suite via scripts/firestore-emulator.sh; the budget guard unit tests for the 50 percent ceiling, the true-up, the stored-bytes level and the 429 quota_exhausted mapping; scripts/infra-policy.sh and tofu fmt -check plus tofu init -backend=false plus tofu validate (measured working in this environment: OpenTofu 1.12.5 with a tracked infra/.terraform.lock.hcl, though init still needs the provider registry on a machine with no populated infra/.terraform cache, which is gitignored); the new preflight schema, its valid and invalid fixtures, and the ledger test passing with zero preflight records; the .gitleaks.toml allowlist extension for .agents/v2/preflight/ with a positive control per docs/architecture/validation.md section 6; and the deploy workflow repairs. The deploy workflow repairs are three: correct the jetify-com/devbox-install-action pin from 22c0f5500b14df4ea357ce673fbd4ced940ed6a1, which does not exist upstream, to 22b0f5500b14df4ea357ce673fbd4ced940ed6a1 as ci.yml already uses; replace the apply step's tofu apply -auto-approve -var-file=... with applying the saved plan produced by the plan step after asserting its sha256 equals the approved preflight record's target.plan_digest; and add scripts/workflow-pins.sh, wired into make check, asserting that for every uses: owner/repo@<sha> # <version> line across .github/workflows the mapping from (owner/repo, version) to sha is unique, since actionlint cannot tell that a pinned revision does not exist upstream but a disagreement between two workflows pinning the same action version is exactly the observable defect. V2-014 is the only place the following may be claimed, and none of it may be substituted by local runs: a real apply against a real project, real drift detection, real IAP authentication and its negative case, real Firestore contention and IAM denial, observed instance_count and billable_instance_time zero during idle, observed Cloud Monitoring operation counts compared with the app's own quota document, observed stored bytes, and a completed revision rollback. Emulator success is never reported as real Firestore verification, tofu validate is never reported as apply, and a passing budget unit test is never reported as live budget enforcement; docs/operations/v2-task-dag.md G3 already rejects the substitution at the gate, and each work order restates it as a constraint.
decisions.rationale: The M2 completion conditions are split by nature: the ones that are statements about configuration and code are decidable locally, and the ones that are statements about a running external system are not decidable at all without that system. Naming the boundary per claim, instead of per milestone, is what prevents an agent from filling the live gap with the nearest green local run. The deploy workflow is in V2-013's scope because docs/operations/v2-task-dag.md section 10 assigns it to V2-012 and V2-013, and because a workflow that cannot start is a local, statically detectable defect; adding the pin-consistency check rather than only fixing the character makes the class of defect detectable instead of the instance.

decisions.decision: Human inputs for V2-014. V2-014 starts as blocked with block_reason external-unavailable: gcp-project; needs: <the list below> and next_owner sol, because gcloud is absent from the machine and from devbox.json (measured) and no project is provisioned or approved. The single list Sol must obtain is: an empty, dedicated project id of the form al-<installation_id>-live that belongs to an organization or Cloud Identity so that an IAP brand can exist, plus the region; a linked billing account, written approval of the monetary ceiling (expected cost zero, staying inside 50 percent of the always-free tiers as quantified in d2), and a Cloud Billing budget with alert thresholds created by the human; the Artifact Registry repository name and region, with the container image already built, pushed and identified by its 64-hex sha256 digest; a private, versioned Cloud Storage bucket for OpenTofu state, created before the first tofu init, since state must not be local for a workflow-driven apply and must never enter Git; the IAP brand or OAuth consent screen, the owner email allowlist, and the exact HTTPS owner origins; and a Workload Identity Federation provider resource name plus a minimum-role deploy service account, distributed only as the GitHub Actions secrets GCP_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_PROVIDER and GCP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT and the variables GCP_DEPLOY_ENABLED, GCP_APPLY_ENABLED, GCP_PROJECT_ID and GCP_TFVARS_FILE, with no service-account key file ever downloaded, committed or handed to an agent. gcloud is deliberately not added to devbox.json; the live read-only observations use curl against the documented REST surfaces (Cloud Resource Manager, Service Usage, Cloud Run Admin v2, Firestore Admin v1, Cloud Monitoring v3, Cloud Scheduler v1) with a short-lived federated token.
decisions.rationale: docs/operations/v2-task-dag.md section 7 fixes the representation of an unavailable external environment, and the block_reason must name what a human has to supply, not merely that something is missing, or the block cannot be cleared without reconstructing this analysis. Every item on the list is something infra/ refuses to create by design or something that cannot be created without a monetary or identity decision, so the list is exactly the boundary between the agent's authority and the owner's. Adding gcloud to devbox.json would change devbox.json and devbox.lock, which docs/policies/README.md says invalidates every component evidence key, so the whole M0 and M1 evidence set would have to be regenerated to gain a CLI that only wraps REST calls that curl can already make.

verification: TFVARS_FILE=<absolute path outside the repository> devbox run --pure -- scripts/infra-plan.sh
cd infra && tofu plan -refresh-only -detailed-exitcode -input=false -var-file=<absolute path outside the repository>

curl -sS -H 'Authorization: Bearer <short-lived federated token>' 'https://monitoring.googleapis.com/v3/projects/<project>/timeSeries?filter=metric.type="run.googleapis.com/container/instance_count"' expecting MAX 0 over the idle window
risks: IAP requires an OAuth brand, and a project outside an organization or Cloud Identity may be unable to have an internal brand at all. Direct-IAP Cloud Run is a deployment invariant in docs/operations/control-plane-production.md and must not be replaced by a spoofable header, so if the supplied project cannot host a brand, V2-014 stops and escalates to product_orchestrator rather than weakening authentication.

The 50 percent Firestore ceiling is genuinely tight: even after the true-up, 10,000 writes per day at the 16-write mutation boundary is 625 mutations per day. If the true-up still cannot support the documented minimum daily operations, the tradeoff between the 50 percent ceiling and a usable plane is a product decision and must be escalated, not silently relaxed.

The exact Cloud Monitoring metric and CLI surface for stored bytes may differ from the assumption at execution time. The evidence must record the metric names and argv actually used; substituting a different observable without recording it would turn a verification into an assertion.

OpenTofu state currently has no backend block, so a workflow-driven apply would use ephemeral local state and try to recreate everything on the next run. The state bucket is a bootstrap precondition that cannot itself be created by this module, and GCP_APPLY_ENABLED must stay false until it exists.

The preflight record contains 64-hex plan and image digests, which the generic-api-key rule flags. The existing .gitleaks.toml allowlist covers only .agents/v2/evidence/, so make secrets will fail on the first preflight record unless V2-013 extends the same AND-scoped allowlist to .agents/v2/preflight/ with a positive control.

tofu init resolves the provider from the registry, so a machine with no populated infra/.terraform cache needs network even for validate. infra/.terraform.lock.hcl is tracked, so the version and hashes are pinned, but offline validation is not guaranteed.

prevent_destroy plus deletion_policy ABANDON means the project can never be returned to empty by OpenTofu. A second clean-project exercise needs a new project, and any attempt to force deletion through tofu state rm would silently orphan the live database.

Changing internal/quota.DefaultBudget touches the assertion in scripts/infra-policy.sh, whose current check is an rg alternation over Shards = 32 and the three 80 percent figures, so it passes if any single branch matches. Retargeting it to the 50 percent figures must convert it into separate fail-closed assertions and prove each one fails when its value is wrong, which is the same OR pitfall docs/architecture/validation.md section 6 records for allowlists.
